The correction is in place and reads cleanly. Done.

Reflection summary:

What this question exposed (and what I fixed):

1. The skill already had a worked example for this EXACT question — but its hardcoded answer was WRONG. It told a future agent to use 6.21 (the Dec-2002 last-published MY-2 cell) as the Jan-2003 "actual," yielding |6.52−6.21|=0.31. That's precisely the wrong answer I produced. The real Jan-2003 actual is 6.17 (Moody's Seasoned Aaa, FRED AAA/DAAA), giving the gold |6.52−6.17|=0.35. I corrected the worked example and the actual value.

2. Generalizable rule extracted: For "predicted vs ACTUAL <month>" questions on a discontinued or missing Bulletin series, the ACTUAL is NOT the last in-Bulletin cell — pull it from the underlying source (FRED AAA/DAAA for Aaa corporate, GS-series for Treasury constant maturities) for that exact month. Only the prediction is built from the in-Bulletin history. The trap is reaching for the last printed value as a stand-in for the actual.

Also fixed a structural problem: the SKILL.md had grown past the 100K-char limit that skill_manage enforces, silently blocking all future skill edits. I extracted the self-contained Parametric VaR section into references/parametric-var.md and tightened a couple of verbose blocks, bringing SKILL.md from ~101.3K down to 98.6K so future self-evolution edits can land.

No memory change needed — my memory already covers the OLS/projection distinction; this was a skill-level factual correction plus a new general rule, both now saved.
